t.1.175.1: Then those tigers among men, the five Pāṇḍava brothers, set out to see Draupadī and that great divine festival.
t.1.175.2: Those tigers among men, scorchers of their foes, having set out together with their mother, saw on the road many brahmins travelling along with their companions.
t.1.175.3: The brahmins said to them, the Pāṇḍavas, who were living as brahmacārins, O king: "Where will you sirs go, or from where have you come?"
t.1.175.5: The Brahmins said: Go this very day to the Pāñcālas, to the dwelling of Drupada; a great svayaṃvara will take place there, one of exceedingly great wealth.
t.1.175.4: Know us, sirs, to be uterine brothers who have come from Ekacakrā, beholders of the gods, travelling together with our mother.
t.1.175.6: We too have set out as one company, bound for that very place; for there a most great festival, wondrous to behold, will take place.
t.1.175.7: The daughter of Yajñasena, the great-souled Drupada, born from the middle of the sacrificial altar, her eyes like lotus petals.
t.1.175.8: Lovely to behold, flawless of limb, delicate and high-minded, she is the sister of the valiant Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the foe of Droṇa.
t.1.175.9: He who was born from the well-kindled fire, mighty-armed and radiant as fire, clad in armor, bearing a sword, with arrows and with a bow.
t.1.175.10: His sister is Draupadī, flawless of limb and slender of waist, whose fragrance, like that of the blue lotus, wafts forth from a krośa away.
t.1.175.12: Kings and princes, performers of sacrifices who gave abundant gifts to the priests, devoted to the study of the Veda, pure, great-souled and firm in their vows.
t.1.175.11: We are going to see that daughter of Yajñasena, for whom the occasion of her svayaṃvara has been set, and that great festival fit for the gods.
t.1.175.13: Kings will gather there, young and handsome, come together from many lands, great chariot-warriors skilled in weapons.
t.1.175.14: There those lords of men, for the sake of victory, will give various gifts: wealth and cows, food to be chewed and food to be eaten, in every way.
t.1.175.15: And having received all that, having seen the svayaṃvara, and having enjoyed the festival, we shall go wherever we please.
t.1.175.16: Actors and bards, dancers, sūtas and māgadhas, and mighty wrestlers will come together from many lands.
t.1.175.17: Having thus satisfied your curiosity, having seen the spectacle and accepted gifts, you great-souled ones will return again together with us.
t.1.175.18: And seeing all of you standing there, handsome and godlike in form, Kṛṣṇā, upon meeting you, might choose one among you as her husband.
t.1.175.20: Sirs, we shall all go together with you to see that supreme great festival of the gods, the maiden's svayaṃvara.
t.1.175.19: This glorious, handsome, mighty-armed brother of yours, if he takes part in the fighting, might by good fortune win much wealth.
